props.title: Alice in Wonderland
props.initialSlug: A young girl's magical journey down the rabbit hole

sections.content: Disney's animated Alice in Wonderland revolutionized surreal animation, transforming Lewis Carroll's literary nonsense into a psychedelic wonderland of impossible physics and dream logic. The film's bold color palette and experimental animation techniques influenced everything from Yellow Submarine (1968) to Coraline (2009). While initially considered a commercial failure, its trippy visuals and jazz-infused soundtrack gained a massive following during the 1960s counterculture movement, cementing its status as Disney's most unconventional animated feature.

sections.content: The film's influence extends deep into modern fantasy cinema. Tim Burton's Alice in Wonderland borrowed the 1951 version's fever-dream aesthetic while adding Gothic elements. Return to Oz (1985) captured similar nightmare fuel with practical effects, while The Science of Sleep (2006) translated Wonderland's dream logic into modern surrealist cinema. The original's character designs, particularly the Cheshire Cat and Mad Hatter, remain definitive versions that subsequent adaptations must either embrace or consciously reject.

Animation techniques pioneered in Alice in Wonderland pushed Disney's boundaries. The tea party sequence's controlled chaos influenced The Sword in the Stone (1963) and The Many Adventures of Winnie the Pooh (1977). Modern animated features like Inside Out (2015) continue drawing from Alice's visualization of abstract concepts and emotional landscapes. SUBHEAD: Impact on Psychedelic Cinema

sections.content: The film's hallucinatory sequences directly inspired the psychedelic era, visible in Yellow Submarine (1968) and Fantastic Planet (1973). Its influence extends to modern mind-bending animations like Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse (2018) and Everything Everywhere All at Once (2022). The Caterpillar's mushroom sequence particularly resonated with counterculture audiences, making Alice a midnight movie staple alongside 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968).
